description.narrative:
Sverige har varit medlem i AFR100 sedan november 2020 och ingår i initiativets ledningsgrupp i 2022. Mellan december 2020 och februari 2023 bidrog Sverige med SEK 20 miljoner till initiativet, tillsammans med AUDA NEPAD och WRI som avtalspartners till Sida. Projektet implementerades enligt plan.
Det nya projektet som nu föreslås överensstämmer med Strategin för Sveriges regionala utvecklingssamarbete med Afrika 2022-2026. Projektet ska under den andra fasen med Sida-stöd till AFR100 ytterligare stärka arbetet med Land Accelerators Program, regional och nationell uppföljning av Forest Landscape Restoration, jämställhetsintegrering samt stöd till kommunikation och synlighet.

Sweden has been a member of AFR100 since November 2020 and has joined the Management Team of the iniative since 2022. From December 2020 to February 2023, Sweden contributed SEK 20 Million for the initiative in which AUDA-NEPAD and WRI were agreement partners of Sida. This project has been implemented as per the plan.
The newly proposed project is in line with the Swedish Regional Development Cooperation Strategy for Sub-Saharan Africa that runs from 2022-2026. The specific areas of intervention under the second phase of Sida support to AFR100 will be further supporting implementation of the Land Accelerators Program, strengthening regional and country level monitoring of Forest Landscape Restoration, Gender Mainstreaming as well as support for communications and visibility.

The Goal of the Project
Under this second phase of cooperation with SIDA, the AUDA-NEPAD/AFR100 Secretariat aims to accelerate the transition from commitments towards implementation by supporting the AFR100 countries in actualizing and scaling up their restoration commitments on the ground through various forest and landscape restoration actions.
The actualization of the countries restoration commitments will contribute to reversing the negative impacts of deforestation and environmental and land degradation, realize healthy, productive landscapes, enhance the livelihoods of smallholder and rural producers, and subsequently build the resilience of rural communities in Africa, who are most susceptible to risk factors.
Specific Objectives
1. Increased support to Women and Youth restoration entrepreneurs: Scaling up the Land Accelerator Programme (LAP).
2. Strengthening Community Resilience and Sustainable Land Restoration: Restore and protect ecosystems, increase carbon sequestration, increase water security, and soil fertility, provide more green jobs and incomes, improve food security and nutrition, and reduce migration.
3. Support to AFR100 Monitoring to crowd in and de-risk investment into FLR, build technical capacity in the country, create green tech jobs, and systematize AFR100 tracking and reporting.

title.narrative: Agreement with Annexes Sida-WRI AFR100 October 2023

description.narrative:
- AFR100 Secretariat achievement - Year 2 Performance (1 June 2024 31 May 2025)
Expanded support to restoration enterprises: Provided business training, mentorship, and innovation grants of USD 5,000 each to 100 women and youth-led restoration enterprises across 19 African countries, strengthening locally led forest landscape restoration initiatives and supporting livelihoods.
Strengthened AFR100 monitoring systems and data infrastructure: Upgraded the AFR100 Monitoring Platform, including development of a new web-based dashboard, improved data visualization tools, and integration of field and remote sensing data. Advanced development of a continental Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) registry and project onboarding system, improving tracking of restoration progress and investment opportunities.
Improved restoration data availability and evidence-based planning: Collected, standardised, and integrated restoration data from Malawi, Kenya, Nigeria, and Tanzania, creating centralised and comparable national FLR databases. Captured restoration data covering hundreds of projects and sites, strengthening national reporting and planning processes.
Built technical capacity of AFR100 member states: Delivered in-country training on restoration monitoring, registry establishment, and data collection in four countries, involving national focal points and technical partners. Supported establishment of Technical Assistance Platforms (TAPs) to institutionalise monitoring and reporting systems and strengthen country ownership.
Enhanced communication and knowledge sharing on restoration: Developed 11 restoration knowledge products and podcasts, documenting best practices and lessons learned. Trained communication officers from 13 AFR100 countries in podcast production, storytelling, and restoration communication strategies to strengthen outreach and behavioral change.
Advanced gender mainstreaming in restoration programming: Trained stakeholders from 13 AFR100 countries on gender-responsive restoration approaches and gender transformative methodologies. Developed and integrated gender indicators and data collection tools into the AFR100 monitoring platform and conducted related training in four countries.
Strengthened continental coordination and partnerships Advanced preparations for the 9th AFR100 Annual Partnership Meeting, including engagement of 34 member countries and establishment of technical, logistics, and communication working groups.
